meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You gave my son a zero before anyone called me, Hale. Why?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what you actually have.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. People write somewhere else and paste it in, Hale.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine, he can bring it. Whatever comes of this, nothing goes on his record and nobody in that class hears a word.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare all the time. That costs him a mark, not the whole essay.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
I'll read the scene myself tonight. What exactly are you proposing for him?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and the final essay; that's what an outline is for. And you still haven't answered me.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, in writing, tonight, Hale. He'll do the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Private, before December 1, and nothing on file.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll check his shifts and answer you in my reply to your email. Put Thursday in it.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, after school and not in front of his class, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require that commitment in writing, along with Thursday the twelfth after school as the proposed date, which I will confirm once I have checked Owen's work schedule. I expect your written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position, agreeing to a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record and still wanting it in writing tonight with Thursday confirmed against his shifts, which is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4.
What moved her: showing the version history with its times and dates on your own screen, because it was specific, tied to Owen's own document, and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: nothing; you owned the early zero in one sentence, never called Owen a liar, and never leaned on the checker score.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, right on top of that kind of night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she said a changed argument between the outline and the essay is just normal drafting, answer that point directly, for instance by offering to hear Owen explain the change himself as procedure 4.1 expects, before you move to the 4.4 offer.
